business_interpretation: Breadth of category engagement signals loyalty and responsiveness to either e-mail variant.

business_interpretation: Marks customers who receive the men's campaign so its effect on purchase can be estimated.

semantic_rationale: Second treatment arm of the randomized experiment, decided before outcomes are observed.
business_interpretation: Identifies customers receiving the women's campaign to measure its incremental effect.
actionability: Directly controllable: choose which customers receive the women's e-mail based on uplift estimates.

semantic_rationale: Combines monetary value and recency: high spenders who bought recently are most engaged.
business_interpretation: Proxy for active customer value; higher values indicate valuable, currently engaged customers.

business_interpretation: Customers with greater past spend are more engaged and more likely to convert after an e-mail.

business_interpretation: Lapsed customers have lower conversion propensity and may need a different message or offer.

actionability: Select the e-mail content (men's, women's, or combined) according to category breadth.

business_interpretation: High spend with recent activity indicates the most responsive customers.
actionability: Use as an RFM-style score to rank customers for sending priority.

semantic_rationale: The randomly assigned campaign is the treatment and is known when the e-mail is sent, so it is available at prediction time.
business_interpretation: Shows whether receiving the men's e-mail changes conversion probability compared with no e-mail.
actionability: Decide which customers to send the men's e-mail to based on the estimated incremental lift.

business_interpretation: Captures the customer's spending level on a diminishing-returns scale, so that going from $50 to $150 counts for more than going from $1050 to $1150.
actionability: Customers can be grouped by value tier to set e-mail frequency or offer size.

semantic_rationale: The dictionary describes recency as dollars spent, but the 1-12 integer range looks like months since last purchase. The flag marks whether the value is above 3, which separates recent from lapsed customers if that reading is correct.
business_interpretation: Separates customers who bought long ago (value above 3) from those who bought recently. This is a classic RFM lapsed-customer indicator.
actionability: Lapsed customers can be targeted with win-back e-mail campaigns.

semantic_rationale: Customers who buy across both categories are broader shoppers and are likely more responsive to either campaign.
business_interpretation: Identifies cross-category shoppers with wider product affinity.
actionability: Cross-category shoppers can get a combined or broader-assortment e-mail instead of a gender-specific one.

semantic_rationale: Counts how many of the three customer-profile flags are active, summarising breadth of engagement with the retailer.
business_interpretation: A rough indicator of how engaged and diverse a customer's relationship with the retailer is.
actionability: Can be used to prioritise customers for broad-appeal campaigns.

semantic_rationale: The dictionary defines visit as holding a store loyalty card, which is a pre-treatment customer attribute. business_interpretation: If the documentation is right, it identifies loyalty members, who tend to be more engaged shoppers.
actionability: If confirmed as a loyalty flag, loyalty members could be targeted differently. Otherwise do not use.
